family.title: Cross-sectional momentum on the point-in-time universe (design draft)

economic.hypothesis: Among liquid USDT spot assets, those with the strongest completed 60-day return (skipping the latest 7 days) continue to outperform the point-in-time universe average over the following week, net of costs.
economic.rationale: Attention-driven and flow-driven trends in crypto persist for weeks because information diffuses unevenly across a large, retail-heavy cross-section, and because arbitrage against such trends is costly in spot-only, no-shorting markets. The skip period removes very short-term reversal (bid-ask bounce, liquidity shocks).
economic.counterparty: Late-reacting retail flow and liquidity takers who sell winners too early or buy losers; the premium is compensation for crash risk (momentum crashes) and for crowded exits, not a free lunch.
expected_failure_modes: Momentum crashes in sharp rebounds after drawdowns wipe out months of gains while long-only cannot hedge.
Transaction costs of weekly turnover (0.15 % per side in the BASE scenario) exceed the gross premium.
The premium exists only in small illiquid assets that the 1 M USDT eligibility filter and the 10 % participation cap exclude.
One market cycle: the result is driven by 2021 and does not repeat; identity breaks and delistings distort history.
economic.falsifiable_prediction: Net of BASE and STRESS costs, the top-quintile portfolio has a higher Sharpe than the point-in-time equal-weight benchmark with a paired-bootstrap lower bound above zero after Holm correction; if not, the hypothesis is rejected.
